title: surge-roster-skill-heatmap-jun-2034
summary: Ad-hoc compact skill heatmap for short-notice surge roster planning. Cross-functional list mapping people to skills, approximate weekly availability, preferred shifts and lightweight confidence notes. Intended for immediate triage when we need to assemble a temporary on-call / surge squad (2–7 day window).
rows: Diego Alvarez | Solutions Engineer | PDT (UTC-7) | model-rollouts, canary deploys | client-integration, kafka | 20 | mornings (08:00-12:00) | yes | strong in small-burst rollouts; limited late-night coverage
Priya Nair | SRE | IST (UTC+5:30) | infra-scaling, autoscale policies | monitoring, incident-runbooks | 30 | evenings (16:00-22:00) | yes | prefers runbook-driven tasks; can lead surge ops
Samir Patel | Applied ML | CET (UTC+1) | quantization, perf profiling | prompt-evals, metrics | 15 | flexible | no | deep model runtime knowledge but limited infra permissions
Maya Chen | Product Ops | PDT (UTC-7) | stakeholder liaison, run coordination | lightweight triage, capacity planning | 35 | mornings | yes | will coordinate handoffs and comms
Lina Gomez | DevRel | EDT (UTC-4) | SDK triage, sample apps | docs, customer-questions | 10 | afternoons | no | good for customer-facing clarifications
Owen Brooks | Platform Eng | PST (UTC-8) | routing policies, fallback logic | k8s, autoscaling | 25 | nights (22:00-02:00) | yes | comfortable taking late windows
Rhea Singh | Security | IST (UTC+5:30) | access controls, KMS | audit logs, compliance | 8 | mornings | no | can triage security gating issues only
Carlos Mendes | Observability | BRT (UTC-3) | tracing, latency analysis | dashboards, alert-tuning | 18 | flexible | yes | can deep-dive latency spikes; needs access to trace-clusters
interpreation_notes: Current quick-pool yields 4 people who can take on-call (Diego, Priya, Maya, Owen, Carlos) but coverage windows are fragmented across timezones.
Highest contiguous coverage (overnights) is weak: only Owen reliably prefers nights. Consider rotating short night shift for PDT/East to cover Latin America evenings.

Skills gap: few contributors comfortable with late-night infra-scaling + model-runtime kernel debugging together. Samir has model runtime expertise but lacks infra perms; consider a temporary sudo path or buddy handoff with Owen.
Security involvement is limited (Rhea 8 hrs/week). For any surge touching keys/audits, pre-approve Rhea's emergent window or create an escalation step.
Total available surge capacity (sum of avail where on-call comfortable) ~108 hrs/week — enough for 3–4 concurrent short tasks if batched; adjust based on expected token load and paging frequency.
derived_actions: Priya to draft a 48-hour surge runbook template (owner: Priya) — due 2034-06-16.
Grant Samir temporary infra-debugging role scoped to debug-lab cluster and log access (owner: Platform Eng) — track via JIRA-OPS-879.
Set up a two-week night shift trial: Owen + rotating PDT volunteer for 22:00-02:00 window. Collect latency/alert noise metrics.
Maya to ping Legal/Security on emergency KMS approval path and capture in runbook.
Add these rows to the central on-call roster sheet and flag any permission blockers in the next standup.
notes: This is intentionally compact — use as a triage-first artifact, not the canonical long-term roster.
Sources: quick Slack poll in #ops-alerts, calendar availability, hallway chats. Validate with each owner before formalizing.
If we move from 48-hour surge to >7 days, transition to the dedicated surge-schedule sheet and assign formal handovers.
